Retail just bet a record on the falling knife.

Individual investors poured $12 billion into semiconductor ETFs in a single week, an all-time record. That was 25% of all the money that went into every ETF over five days, even though chip funds are 1% of total ETF assets.

They did this during the worst month for chip stocks since 2008, a stretch that erased $2.2 trillion and ran the hottest volatility since Covid. The favorites were a memory-chip fund and a triple-leveraged semi fund.

When the crowd pours record cash into the most volatile group in the market to buy a crash, that is conviction and danger in the same trade.

$SMH

The most indebted consumer in the developed world is watching home prices fall.

Australian house prices dropped 0.7% in July, the steepest run of declines since 2022, with Sydney down 1.4%. Yet mortgage debt is still growing: total home loans up 7.5% from a year ago, and investor borrowing up 10.4%, the fastest in over a decade.

Prices down while leverage climbs is how negative equity gets built. Three RBA rate hikes this year are finally biting the household balance sheet. When the most leveraged consumer in the developed world cracks, the wealth effect goes into reverse and spending follows it down.

$EWA

Banks are buying disaster insurance on their own products.

Leveraged and single-stock ETFs ballooned past $200 billion in June before slipping to $160 billion. To survive a one-day 50% drop that would wipe out a 2X fund, dealers are loading up on exotic crash puts. Protection on SK Hynix nearly doubled, from 3.5% in March to 6.5% in May.

When the firms handing out the leverage are paying up for tail insurance, the tail is fat. This is hidden, overlapping leverage stacked across many counterparties, the exact setup that turns one gap-down into a daisy chain reaction of claymore mines.

Foreigners now own a record 32.4% of Japan's stock market, the highest since Tokyo began tracking it in 1970.

The yen carry trade that funded that bid broke after April 2025. The yen stopped tracking the US-Japan rate gap. Now it trades on Japan's fiscal mess, near a 40-year low, and a $70B intervention plus a BOJ hike couldn't stop the slide.  

The marginal owner of the Nikkei is foreign money, priced in the shakiest yen in decades. When the yen cracks, foreigners are the sellers, and they hold a third of the tape. $EWJ

The bond market is done waiting on the Fed to explain itself.

The 30-year Treasury just hit a 19-year high. The 2yr/30yr curve bear-steepened toward 100 basis points in weeks as traders dumped the long end. Options desks are now betting the 10-year tags 4.9% by August 21 and the 30-year clears 5.4%.

Warsh went dark, floated fewer Fed meetings, and offered no framework to fight inflation. So the market is repricing term premium on its own.

A 19-year high in the long bond is a higher discount rate on every stock, house, and corporate loan in America. When the bond vigilantes take the wheel, risk assets lose their floor.

$TLT
